note: Places a human has looked at and confirmed, so the geocode audit stops asking. Each says why the obvious-looking alternative is the wrong one — because the audit's heuristic (a much larger place of the same name exists elsewhere) is a prompt, not an answer.

middelburg.why: Middelburg in the Eastern Cape, population 22,380. The audit points at Middelburg in Mpumalanga, which is nine times larger and 770 km away — and is not where the Booyzen family is. Size is not relevance.

prato.why: Prato Carnico in the Val Degano, which carries the Friulian name Pratu and 62 register volumes. The audit points at Prato in Tuscany, 195,000 people and 323 km away. This is the Carnia ground and the small one is right.

bradwell.why: Four English Bradwells — Derbyshire, Essex, Norfolk, Buckinghamshire — and the D'Arcy archive's ground is Somerset and Kent, neither of them near any. Left where the geocoder put it, in Buckinghamshire, and flagged rather than guessed at.

miguel-hidalgo.why: Thirty-six places in Mexico carry this name. The large one is a borough of Mexico City; ours is a small settlement 234 km away, and the coordinates came from FamilySearch's own catalogue rather than from a geocoder here. Mexico is not a ground this project has worked, so this is left where its source put it and flagged rather than moved on a guess.
